title: Hichilema re-election expected to preserve Zambia's copper policy
gist: Hakainde Hichilema's decisive re-election win in Zambia is expected to preserve policy continuity for the country's 2024 critical minerals strategy and copper beneficiation agenda, at a time when Zambian copper output is growing double digits and the government targets a near-tripling of production by 2031.

themes.theme: Zambian political continuity and copper policy

insights.claim: Hakainde Hichilema won re-election as Zambia's president with a decisive margin (nearly 3 million votes, over 1.1 million votes ahead of runner-up Brian Mundubile of the NRPUP, comfortably clearing the 50% threshold to avoid a run-off), removing near-term political uncertainty for the country's mining sector.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A decisive win (rather than a contested or narrow result) lowers the probability of near-term policy reversal risk for investors exposed to Zambian copper supply chains.
insights.quote: Hakainde Hichilema was declared president-elect of Zambia on 18 August.

insights.claim: Benchmark's lead policy and geopolitical analyst expects the election result to deliver policy and geopolitical continuity, including continuation of the beneficiation agenda set out in Zambia's 2024 critical minerals strategy.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Continuity of the beneficiation (local processing) agenda affects whether foreign miners can keep exporting raw copper concentrate or will face increasing pressure/incentives to invest in domestic smelting and refining capacity in Zambia.
insights.quote: The result is expected to deliver policy and geopolitical continuity, including the continuation of the beneficiation agenda set out in Zambia's 2024 critical minerals strategy

insights.claim: Copper accounts for around three-quarters of the total value of Zambia's exports, making the country's political stability directly material to global copper supply forecasts and to companies and countries dependent on Zambian copper for battery and EV supply chains.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Zambia's export concentration in copper means any future political or policy shock there would flow directly through to global copper supply and pricing, relevant to battery and EV materials investors.
insights.quote: Copper is a crucial export for Zambia, accounting for around three-quarters of the total value of the country's exports.

insights.claim: Zambia's mined copper production in 2026 is estimated at 901kt, an 11% increase over the prior year, according to Benchmark's Copper Service.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Double-digit annual production growth signals Zambia is already scaling output ahead of its stated targets, a positive supply-side data point for copper availability forecasts.
insights.quote: Mined production in 2026 is estimated at 901kt, a healthy growth of 11% over last year, as assessed by Benchmark's Copper Service.

insights.claim: The Zambian government is targeting copper output of 3 million tonnes per annum by 2031, which would be more than triple the estimated 2026 production level of 901kt within five years.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A 3x production ramp target by 2031 is an aggressive goal investors should track against actual investment and permitting progress — Zambia's political continuity is a precondition for, but not a guarantee of, hitting this target.
insights.quote: The Zambian government is aiming to increase output to 3Mtpa by 2031.
